newsitem.title: ITALY: Fresh problems seen in Italian metalworkers' row.
newsitem.headline: Fresh problems seen in Italian metalworkers' row.

text.p: Italian trades unions on Sunday accused employers in the engineering and metalworking industry of putting fresh obstacles in the way of a settlement to their protracted dispute over pay.
Union leaders had hoped for a deal by Sunday in the months-old dispute but said after a meeting that they believed it was now up to the government to decide how to carry negotiations forward.

Talks between unions and employers resumed last Monday for the first time in more than a month to try to end the dispute, which involves some 1.7 million workers in a sector which accounts for 40 percent of industrial output.
Newspapers on Sunday reported that unions and the employers' group Federmeccanica had agreed in principle to a 30-month national contract to replace a two-year contract that expired last June.
But union leaders said Federmeccanica was also insisting that any supplementary factory-level agreements should last for three years to limit the impact on labour costs.
"We have already clarified what our positions are," said Sergio Cofferati, leader of the CGIL labour confederation.
"Federmeccanica has introduced obstacles to the negotiations and it's up to them to remove them," he said.
Any deal is likely to set the tone for other pay accords and prove crucial to Italy's hopes of containing inflation.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, who has been shepherding the negotiations, appealed to both sides to show a sense of responsibility.
"It would be very risky indeed to prolong this," Treu told Italian radio. "It could lead to a further rise in tension and that is the last thing we need."
